novelty.claim: MIL-CREDA extends Conditional Rényi $\alpha$-Entropy Domain Adaptation (CREDA) to multiple-instance learning: each subject is a bag of EEG windows, the label is observed only at the bag level, and adaptation runs between labelled source bags and unlabelled target bags (r38, opening paragraph). The protocol (v45) tests it on the EEG modality of the BALLADEER ADHD dataset across level, task and device shifts against eight external comparators. No campaign result exists yet; every hypothesis below is pending.
novelty.rationale: This is the existing proposal, not an empirically justified novelty verdict.

qualitative_not_applicable: Full-campaign qualitative analysis is not available yet. Existing preprocessing diagnostic figures remain accessible separately and are not a substitute for that analysis.
limitations: No campaign hypothesis has been empirically decided.
The source filename classifies this record as full, but Experimental_AGREED.md remains an unapproved placeholder.
The existing timing probe names v40 and explicitly defers canonical timing.json until epoch caps are fixed.

Declared limitation (plausibility screening, sota-pool/screening-report-2026-11-03.md, tension C4-T): class-conditional alignment can degrade when target class proportions differ from the source, because target pseudo-labels become unreliable (SPDIM 2411.07249; CCA-LSC 2412.20337). The global term weights target bags by pseudo-label confidence; no experiment isolates this case.

Declared limitation (tension C6-T): EEG multiple-instance learning is more sensitive to subject scarcity than to instance scarcity (BridgeMIL 2607.27274), and the bag-level terms are estimated over few bags (31 source training bags in L1->L11, Results/timing_probe.json); no experiment varies the number of subjects.
